_note: Residual adjustments to a player's win probability, indexed by bucket. Fitted on walk-forward residuals (never on the data that fitted the ratings), shrunk toward zero by n/(n+400), and validated on rolling time folds with the adjustment applied ANTISYMMETRICALLY and in LOG-ODDS, which is how price.py applies them. Worth -0.00541 nats out of sample (2026-09-15, 7-day cadence, age-dependent prior, refreshed archive; -0.00738 with the flat own prior, -0.00807 at 21 days, -0.00999 at 91 -- each improvement to the rating layer leaves the curves less to correct) at the shipped magnitude (k=1), 4 folds of 4; k=1.25 is within 0.0003 of it and the scale chosen on each fold's train half scores worse, so the natural value stays. Cost of dropping: entry +0.00100, age +0.00091, event_gwp +0.00090, resid_prior +0.00088, matches_28d +0.00083, form_spw +0.00026, event_sets_lost +0.00022, home +0.00015 -- entry is now the largest and age has more than halved, which is the age-dependent prior doing what it was built to do. EIGHT curves since 2026-09-12: entry (how the player got into the draw: qualifiers beat their price, protected-ranking entrants miss it) adds -0.00058 on top of the seven and costs +0.00058 to drop; live prices take it from the --entry flag / the app control, or from the player's earlier rows at the event when the archive carries a code, else unknown and no adjustment (the reconstructed feed carries the code since 2026-09-14). Measured 2026-09-12 and REJECTED in company: resid_365 (the player's residual over the last 365 days only, -0.00131 alone, +0.00092 when added: a substitute for resid_prior) and resid_surface (the residual on this surface only, -0.00038 alone, +0.00119 when added). Refitted 2026-09-11 against residuals priced through the CLI's own path (price.serve_probs: surface with the recent-form carry-over, in-event update, air density, the qual/Challenger supplement, age multipliers (0.50, 0.85); three-stage serve OFF). SEVEN curves: the seventh, resid_prior, is the player's own mean walk-forward residual over their prior matches, shrunk by n/(n+40) -- does this player beat the point model -- split-half reliability 0.39 for players with 40+ rows; it adds -0.00166 on top of the other six and costs +0.00166 to drop; live prices read it from data/player_traits.json. Cost of dropping each from the set: age +0.00255, resid_prior +0.00166, matches_28d +0.00146, event_gwp +0.00092, form_spw +0.00074, home +0.00018, event_sets_lost +0.00016. Measured 2026-09-11 and REJECTED in company: rank_gap (+0.00077 when added), seeded (+0.00035), bo5_resid_prior (+0.00007), log_rank (-0.00012, not worth a stale live input), elo_vs_model and opp_lefty (hurt alone), bo_diff_prior (hurts alone); entry type ADDS -0.00047 but cannot be known live before a player's first match at an event, so it waits for a draw source. REJECTED, each because it makes the SET worse or adds nothing: event_matches (raw wins banked -- the signal is margin, not count), bp_form (break points saved: clutch is noise), event_opp_rank, career_matches, career_pts, home_km, rank_change, peak_gap. The last three are all the same trend signal `age` already carries.
